title: Fire Safety Awareness
blurb: The assembly point, what to do if you find a fire or hear the alarm, and keeping escape routes clear.
siteNotes: Confirm the assembly point is still the car park at the bottom of the Orangery, and that it is the same for the marquee and events.
Where the nearest break-glass call points and fire exits are in each department (your manager will show you).
Who the Duty Manager is on each shift.
legalNotes: Duties to prepare for fire, provide exits, alarms and training: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2005/1541
CHECK: assembly point (car park at the bottom of the Orangery) is taken from the trainer as a venue fact; please confirm it is current.

CHECK: the trainer says to call 999 as well as raising the alarm. Many fire procedures have the alarm calling the Fire Service automatically or a manager making the call; confirm what your fire procedure says about who dials 999.

cards.title: Fire Safety Awareness
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say where the assembly point is
- know what to do if you find a fire or hear the alarm
- keep fire doors and exits as they should be

cards.title: Know the plan before you need it
cards.body:
If there is a fire, the seconds count and there is no time to start wondering what to do. Every one of us needs to know the plan.

> At Black Horse Beamish the assembly point is the car park at the bottom of the Orangery. Whatever happens, that is where we all go to be counted.

items.title: Fire
items.text: Seconds count, so know the plan.

items.title: Exit
items.text: Go to the nearest fire exit.

items.title: Assembly point
items.text: Car park at the bottom of the Orangery.

cards.title: If YOU discover a fire
cards.body:
Do not tackle it first. Raise the alarm straight away.

Only ever try to put a fire out if it is small, you have been trained and your escape route is behind you. If you are in any doubt at all, get out.

items.title: Raise the alarm
items.text: Operate the nearest break-glass call point.

items.title: Move guests
items.text: Calmly towards the nearest fire exit.

cards.title: If you HEAR the alarm
cards.body:
Treat it as the real thing every time. Never assume it is a test. Stop what you are doing, help guests to the nearest exit and go.

Close doors behind you as you leave. It slows the spread of fire and smoke and can buy people vital time.

right.title: Do not
items: Stop for your coat or phone

cards.title: Stay out
cards.body:
The Duty Manager runs the roll call and deals with the Fire Service, so report to them at the assembly point.

Nobody goes back inside for any reason until the Fire Service or the Duty Manager says it is safe.

items.title: Go to the assembly point
items.text: Get out and head there to be counted.

items.title: Wait
items.text: Stay out until you are told it is safe.

cards.title: Keep fire doors shut and exits clear
cards.body: Day to day, the basics save lives. Keep fire doors closed and never wedge them open. Keep exits and escape routes clear. A blocked exit could cost a life.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- If you find a fire, raise the alarm first
- Treat every alarm as real, and do not use the lifts
- Close doors behind you and go to the assembly point
- Stay out until the Fire Service or Duty Manager says it is safe
- Never wedge fire doors open or block exits

cards.q: Where is the assembly point at Black Horse Beamish?
options: The nearest fire exit inside the building
The car park at the bottom of the Orangery
The reception desk in the hotel lobby
Anywhere outside that feels safe to you
cards.why: Whatever happens, the whole team heads to the car park at the bottom of the Orangery to be counted.

cards.q: If you discover a fire, the first thing to do is try to put it out.
cards.why: Do not tackle it first. Raise the alarm straight away.

cards.q: If you discover a fire, what should you do first?
cards.why: Raise the alarm straight away by operating the nearest break-glass call point.

cards.q: You should always treat the fire alarm as real, never as a test.
cards.why: Treat the alarm as the real thing every time and never assume it is a test.

cards.q: It's fine to use the lift to evacuate if it's quicker.
cards.why: Do not use the lifts. Go to the nearest fire exit.

cards.q: When can you go back into the building?
options: When the alarm has stopped ringing
When the building looks safe again
When your colleagues start going back in
When the Fire Service or Duty Manager says it is safe
cards.why: Nobody goes back inside for any reason until the Fire Service or the Duty Manager says it is safe. The alarm stopping is not enough.

cards.q: Why should you close doors behind you as you leave?
options: It slows the spread of fire and smoke
cards.why: Closed doors slow the spread of fire and smoke and can buy people vital time.

cards.q: You should only tackle a fire if it's small, you're trained, and your exit is behind you.
cards.why: All three must be true, and if in any doubt you just get out.

cards.q: Who runs the roll call and deals with the Fire Service?
cards.why: Report to the Duty Manager at the assembly point. They run the roll call and deal with the Fire Service.

cards.q: Fire doors can be wedged open to help with airflow.
cards.why: Keep fire doors closed and never wedge them open. They only protect people when shut.
